shadows.purpose: Separate a focused detail or editor from the calendar.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: Lift the calendar paper off the neutral workspace.

shadows.name: glass-contact
shadows.purpose: Lift a glass pane by contact only. The hairline border declares the edge; a wide shadow on top of it would be a ghost card.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Separate a popover or dropdown from the surface beneath it.

motion.name: detail-enter
motion.purpose: Gentle enlargement from the selected task or event.

motion.name: detail-exit
motion.purpose: Fade an inert clone after releasing dialog state.

narrative.overview: A month-first calendar with quiet navigation and tasks within reach. The desktop is one window: three glass panes around a paper calendar, floating on a washed canvas. The toolbar answers two questions 鈥?where am I on the left, what am I doing on the right.

rules.name: Neutral ramp
rules.body: The surface ramp is grey, not green-tinted. A tinted ramp made the whole app read as one green wash and dulled the accent; the green survives only in the ink that text is drawn in.

rules.name: Colour carries the block
rules.body: Event color rides a 46% block over the paper on desktop (30% in dark mode), so the grid lines and day numbers stay legible while the category stays unmistakable. All-day and multi-day bars keep their solid fill.

rules.name: Glass where it separates
rules.body: The toolbar, the navigation column, the task panel and the sign-in card are glass because they float over other content. The calendar itself stays paper.

rules.name: One window, three panes
rules.body: Header, navigation column and task panel share one glass material; the calendar is the paper inside that window. A transparent navigation column made the application read as three and a half pieces.

rules.name: Canvas wash
rules.body: The canvas under the window is a two-stop vertical wash, light above and deeper below, one step under the chrome and two under the paper. A flat single-colour canvas made the window float on nothing.

rules.name: Two groups in the toolbar
rules.body: Left answers where am I (today, stepping arrows, period title, view switcher); right answers what am I doing (search, tasks, settings, account). The switcher follows the title because it describes the same thing the title describes.

rules.name: Indigo means one thing
rules.body: Indigo marks the primary action, today and the current selection. Hover states are neutral 鈥?tinting every icon hover made the toolbar glow.

rules.name: Readable pastels
rules.body: Use dark ink on bright event fills.

rules.name: No side-tabs
rules.body: A saturated stripe down the edge of a card reads as an alert, not as decoration. Carry state in the fill, the type, or a border of the surface ramp instead.

dos: Preserve custom settings and native keyboard access.
Keep the last stylesheet in the cascade honest: a rule added there silently beats an earlier @media block, so scope it to the widths it was designed for.
Let a control title hug its own text; stretch it only when it is a flexible label.
donts: Do not spread blur across calendar content.
Do not rely on pastel color alone for completion, selection or keyboard focus.
Do not put a view switcher between two tools that belong together.
